reason: The picture says pancreatic cells release insulin when blood glucose is higher, matching the first goal.
expectation: The higher-glucose blood will prompt the cells to release insulin.

effect: Insulin is now in the blood and can carry the message toward muscle.
reaction: The route to muscle makes the next step clearer.
reason: The muscle hotspot shows receptors for blood-carried insulin, matching the goal of storing glucose in muscle.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin will signal the muscle to take in glucose, possibly using the glucose already beside it.

effect: Insulin and nearby glucose produced a muscle carbohydrate store, completing the first goal; the hormone acts as a message rather than becoming part of the store.
reaction: It was helpful to see insulin stay outside while glucose became stored material.
reason: The pancreatic cell picture links lower blood glucose to release of the other hormone, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The lower-glucose blood will prompt the cells to release the liver's chemical message.

effect: Lower blood glucose prompted release of a hormone that carries a message to the liver.
reaction: The label makes its purpose clear.
reason: The hormone's route leads to the liver, where the existing carbohydrate store can supply glucose.
expectation: The hormone will signal the liver to break down stored carbohydrate and release glucose.

effect: The liver used its stored carbohydrate to release glucose into the blood, completing the remaining goal. The release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the earlier liver store used between meals.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using insulin at the muscle was most worthwhile: the picture showed glucose becoming stored material while insulin stayed outside as a message.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the two pancreatic messages felt somewhat repetitive, although the different glucose levels made their purposes clear.

surprise.text: I was interested that the muscle stores glucose for its own later work, while the liver can release glucose into the blood.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals connected each message to its target.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter because connecting the two hormone signals to what happens to stored glucose was clear and satisfying.
